title: Use of the Philips Visual Patient Avatar in Perioperative Monitoring in Cardiac Surgery—A Case Series.
summary: During heart surgery, anaesthesia teams must monitor many vital signs at the same time. The Philips Visual Patient Avatar is a monitor display that shows these values as an animated figure using colour, shape and movement, so that changes can be recognised faster, even at a glance. This display is already used routinely at University Hospital Bonn. In this study, we record screenshots during about 20 heart operations to document which circulatory situations the avatar shows, and we anonymously ask the care team about its usefulness and ease of use. Patient treatment does not change.
conditions: Patients undergoing cardiac surgery (perioperative haemodynamic monitoring)

interventions.name: Observational group: Adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery who receive perioperative monitoring with the Philips Visual Patient Avatar (VPA) as part of routine clinical care.
